subject: Maths
central_question: How can fractional quantities be represented, compared, converted, added, and subtracted meaningfully?
in_scope_units: 7.2 Fractional Units as Parts of a Whole
7.4 Marking Fraction Lengths on the Number Line
banned_topics: General multiplication and division of fractions

known_pitfalls.claim: A larger denominator always makes a larger fraction.
known_pitfalls.correction: For unit fractions of one whole, a larger denominator makes smaller parts.
Make denominators equal, then add numerators and keep the denominator.

known_pitfalls.claim: Every fraction greater than 1 has a non-zero fractional part.
known_pitfalls.correction: For example, 8/4 is exactly the whole number 2.

recommended_example_progression: Use equal sharing and paper strips for unit fractions.
Place fractions on the number line.
Convert between improper fractions and mixed numbers.
Use a fraction wall for equivalence and lowest terms.
Compare, add, and subtract using common denominators.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: Use the Figure it Out tasks in Sections 7.1–7.8, including the final Brahmagupta-method subtraction and word problems.
